shortDescription: NEW YORK, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Actinium Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NYSE American: ATNM) ("Actinium" or the "Company"), a pioneer in the development of targeted radiotherapies, today announced inducement equity awards to Matt David, M.D., the Company's newly appointed Chief Financial Officer, a…

children: (NYSE American: ATNM) ("Actinium" or the "Company"), a pioneer in the development of targeted radiotherapies, today announced inducement equity awards to Matt David, M.D., the Company's newly appointed Chief Financial Officer, and Sean Maenpaa, the Company's newly appointed Senior Vice President, Business Development.

In connection with Dr. David's appointment, on October 14, 2026 the Company granted Dr. David a non-qualified stock option to purchase 250,000 shares of the Company's common stock at an exercise price of $0.97 per share, equal to the closing price of Actinium's common stock on the NYSE American on October 14, 2026. The option has a ten-year term; 28% of the shares underlying the option vest on the first anniversary of the grant date, and the remainder vest in equal monthly installments of 2% of the shares underlying the option over the following 36 months. Dr. David was also granted 250,000 restricted stock units ("RSUs"), of which 125,000 vest in three equal annual installments on the first, second and third anniversaries of the grant date and 125,000 vest in full on the third anniversary of the grant date, as well as up to 75,000 RSUs that vest upon the achievement of specified corporate milestones.

In connection with Mr. Maenpaa's appointment, on October 12, 2026 the Company granted Mr. Maenpaa a non-qualified stock option to purchase 40,000 shares of the Company's common stock at an exercise price of $1.06 per share, equal to the closing price of Actinium's common stock on the NYSE American on October 12, 2026. The option has a ten-year term; 28% of the shares underlying the option vest on the first anniversary of the grant date, and the remainder vest in equal monthly installments of 2% of the shares underlying the option over the following 36 months. Mr. Maenpaa was also granted 20,000 RSUs that vest in three equal annual installments on the first, second and third anniversaries of the grant date, and 50,000 RSUs that vest on the third anniversary of the grant date, subject to the fulfillment of certain corporate milestones.

Vesting of each award is subject to the executive's continued service with the Company through the applicable vesting date. The awards were granted outside of the Company's Amended and Restated 2019 Stock Plan as an inducement material to each executive's entering into employment with the Company in accordance with Section 711(a) of the NYSE American Company Guide, and are subject to the terms of the Actinium Pharmaceuticals, Inc. 2026 Employment Inducement Award Plan and the applicable award agreements.

Actinium is a pioneer in targeted radiotherapies designed to improve outcomes for patients with cancer. The company employs a biology-driven approach to develop differentiated radiopharmaceuticals for solid tumors and hematologic malignancies. Its mission is to transform cancer treatment through innovative radioconjugates that maximize therapeutic efficacy while minimizing toxicity to healthy tissue by combining expertise in tumor biology, translational medicine, and radiochemistry. Since inception, Actinium has focused on developing innovative radiotherapies. Its pipeline reflects this strategy across three areas: (1) solid tumor therapeutics including ATNM-400 and Actimab-A with pan-tumor potential; (2) Actimab-A as a therapeutic backbone for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) in collaboration with the National Cancer Institute (NCI); and (3) targeted conditioning agents including Iomab-B for bone marrow transplant and Iomab-ACT for cell and gene therapy conditioning. ATNM-400 targets a novel antigen distinct from PSMA and has demonstrated preclinical activity across metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and breast cancer, and is being evaluated in a first-in-human Phase 1 study in mCRPC. Actimab-A has shown improved survival in relapsed/refractory AML with CLAG-M and is advancing toward a Phase 2/3 trial, with additional development ongoing through a CRADA with the NCI. Actinium is also advancing preclinical solid tumor programs and holds ~250 patents and patent applications, including intellectual property related to cyclotron-based production of Ac-225.
